vcloze1.h1: This sentence asks you to think back. Which bank word means that?
vcloze1.why: reflect means to think carefully about something that happened.

vcloze2.h1: Finishing a book is a reason for a party. Which bank word fits?
vcloze2.why: celebrate means to mark something with joy.

vcloze3.h1: The Whipping Boy is a long story with chapters. Which bank word names that?
vcloze3.why: a novel is a long story with characters, plot and theme.

match.reflect: Reflect is about thinking back. Look for that meaning.
match.celebrate: Celebrate is about joy. Look for the meaning about honoring something.

match.memorable: Memorable has memory inside it. Look for the meaning about remembering.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. This is our last day with The Whipping Boy. Today you read your comparison paragraph out loud, and you look back at the whole book. What moment will you remember most?
transcripts.guide1: Word study review. Roll struct words, hunt for pronouns in the wrong job, and roll compound words.
transcripts.guide2: No new chapters today. Think about which boy changed the most, and what you would tell the author.
transcripts.guide3: Today you read your comparison paragraph out loud. Then write what you noticed.

notes.wordParts: The root struct means build. construct = to build together. structure = something built. instruct = to build knowledge in someone.
notes.grammar: A pronoun takes the place of a noun. Doing the action: I, he, she, we, they. Getting the action: me, him, her, us, them. Showing whose: my, his, her, their.
notes.spelling: A compound word is two small words joined into one: rain + bow = rainbow. Read each part on its own, then blend them. A long word is not always a compound word.
notes.wgrd: Good readers remember a book after they close it. Think about where the characters started and where they ended.
vocab: to think carefully about something that happened
a long story with characters, plot and theme

What a picture that sentence makes! Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Read the poem out loud again. Then answer the question in the box.
mods.script: Here's the Rossetti poem again. This time, think about why she wrote it this way. She could have just said, don't step on bugs. Instead the cricket is cheerful, and the gnat dances. Which way makes you care more? Answer the question in the box.

mods.todo: Tap Roll the Dice. Say what the word means. Tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six words.
mods.script: Riddle time. I'm six letters long. I hide inside big words. And I mean build. What am I? Struct! Roll a word, find struct inside it, and say what the whole word means, out loud. Then tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six.

mods.todo: Fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank. Tap Check My Work. Then play the matching game.
mods.script: One more word before we say goodbye to this book. Farewell. Fare, plus well. It means goodbye, and good luck! Read each sentence with a bank word in the blank. If it sounds right and makes sense, keep it. Then play the matching game.

mods.todo: Tap the wrong word, or tap No mistake. Then tap See the answers and answer the question in the box.
mods.script: Spot the mistake with me. The boy lost him hat. Him hat? The hat belongs to the boy, so it's his hat. A pronoun in the wrong job sounds funny when you say it out loud. Read each sentence out loud. Tap the wrong word, or tap No mistake.

mods.todo: Tap Roll the dice. Say the two small words. Tap Check my answer. Roll all six.
mods.script: Roll one with me. Toothbrush! Say it slowly. Tooth. Brush. Two small words make one big word. Now roll all six. Say each word out loud, then say the two small words that make it.
Here's the very last thing the king says. If you boys decide to run away again, take me with you. At the start of the book, would you ever have pictured the king saying that? What changed?

mods.todo: Read the two questions. Then look back through the whole book.
mods.script: There are no new chapters today. Read the two Pause and Think questions first. Then think back over the whole book. Which boy changed the most? And if you could tell the author one thing, what would it be? Then do the Read Like a Writer box.

mods.todo: Pick Explorer or Scholar. Answer the three questions in full sentences.
mods.script: Now look back at your own writing, and answer in full sentences. One, do you still believe the claim in your opinion paragraph? Two, copy your strongest sentence, and tell why it's strong. Three, what moment will you remember longest? For a challenge, pick Scholar, and add one more detail.

virtue.name: courage
virtue.title: Courage Watch: Did they show courage?

items.t: In Chapter 3, Jemmy asks, “Ain’t you afraid o’ the dark?” The prince answers, “Lies!”
items.why: He hides that he is scared instead of saying so.

items.t: In Chapter 17, when Petunia roars, Hold-Your-Nose Billy charges off into the river.
In Chapter 20, Jemmy has a price on his head, but he tells Betsy, “Better do what he says,” and goes along with the prince’s plan.
items.why: He trusts his friend, even though it is a big risk.
